Chapter Eight: Measuring What Matters—Tracking Progress Toward a Meaningful Life
You know, in business, we talk a lot about KPIs—those key performance indicators that help us keep score and see how we're doing against our goals.
But when it comes to your personal life, things aren’t always so clear-cut. How do you measure something as big and fuzzy as fulfillment, or happiness, or real growth?
Here’s where it all starts: you’ve got to figure out what really matters to you.
Is it the quality of your relationships? Your personal growth? Maybe your health, or the ways you give back to others?
Once you know what’s truly important, you can start to track your progress in simple, meaningful ways.
Think about it like having a dashboard in front of you. Instead of trying to monitor every single thing, you focus on just a handful of gauges that really reflect your core values.
For example, you might pay attention to how many real, meaningful conversations you’re having with loved ones each week. Or maybe you look at the time you spend on creative projects, or learning something new.
Even something like how often you exercise or practice self-care—these are all great ways to keep things on track.
The point isn’t to be perfect. It’s more about awareness.
These little check-ins give you feedback. They help you spot trends and make changes where you need to. Say you notice you haven’t spent much time with friends lately—that’s your cue to reach out, reconnect, and bring things back into balance.
But here’s something to pay attention to: don’t just measure what’s easy to count.
Some of the most important pieces of life—like your sense of purpose, or inner peace—aren’t numbers at all.
That’s where journaling or regular reflection comes in. Or maybe you have honest conversations with someone you trust. These are powerful ways to notice how you’re growing in those harder-to-measure areas.
So how do you put this into practice?
Try setting aside a little time each week—or even just once a month—for a personal review. Use a simple checklist, or jot down a few notes in a journal about what went well and what you found challenging.
And don’t forget to celebrate those small wins along the way. They matter more than you might think.
If things don’t go as planned, that’s okay too. Every setback is a chance to learn and adjust.
At the end of the day, measuring what matters isn’t about chasing numbers. It’s about staying true to your values and intentions, so you don’t drift off course.
It keeps you aligned, motivated, and growing—one step at a time.
